about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority
channels.legal_basis: NPDES permit NM0022250 (EPA Region 6): the 24-hour and five-day noncompliance reports of 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6), to EPA
channels.note: Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority reports noncompliance to EPA Region 6 under its permit; EPA publishes the reports filed electronically in its overflow tables, read by the echo-sewer-overflow feed (no report under its permits in the 2026-11-04 extract). channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (ECHO)
channels.note: EPA's sewer overflow and bypass event tables (NPDES electronic reporting): the reports New Mexico's permittees file electronically with EPA, and the Navajo Nation's under its own permits. 2026-11-04 extract: 2 reports under New Mexico permits, both the Town of Taos's (2026), and 6 Navajo Nation reports located in New Mexico (3 Shiprock, 2024 to 2025; 3 under Window Rock's permit, 2026, two of them at the lift station by Navajo, New Mexico); a median 4 days from start to receipt. EPA's collection-system table lists 55 New Mexico permits, Albuquerque, Santa Fe and Las Cruces among them, but no other has filed a report. (research/nm/report.md §2.2)

channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Region 6 (noncompliance reports)
channels.legal_basis: 40 CFR 122.41(l)(6) and (m)(3): the permit's 24-hour and five-day noncompliance reports to the permitting authority
channels.note: Reports New Mexico's permittees send EPA Region 6 outside its electronic tool (by telephone, e-mail or letter) do not reach EPA's tables, and no web channel found publishes them. The electronic reporting deadline for sewer overflows passed on 2025-12-21, yet of the 55 New Mexico permits EPA lists with a collection system only Taos has filed. (research/nm/profile.json barriers)

channels.name: New Mexico Environment Department (discharge notices under 20.6.2.1203 NMAC)
channels.legal_basis: 20.6.2.1203.A(1) NMAC: "As soon as possible after learning of such a discharge, but in no event more than twenty-four (24) hours thereafter, any person in charge of the facility shall orally notify the chief of the ground water quality bureau of the department"; (3) written notice within one week; (6) a corrective-action report within 15 days
channels.note: The notice goes to NMED's Ground Water Quality Bureau by telephone only at first, then in writing within a week, with a corrective-action report in 15 days; it binds every person in charge of a facility, public or private, off tribal land. NMED publishes no list of the notices and no web form was found; the notices reach the public only through a records request. (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/new-mexico/N-M-Admin-Code-SS-20.6.2.1203; research/nm/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: New Mexico Environment Department (HABs Mapper)
channels.note: NMED's harmful algal bloom advisory map: each monitored lake or river station's latest result and its status (WATCH, WARNING or DANGER, or monitored with no advisory), read from the map's public layer (40 stations on 2026-11-07: 8 WATCH, 6 WARNING). Blooms, not sewage. Advisories follow NMED's HAB Advisory Guidance; no law requires them. (research/nm/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: New Mexico Environment Department (harmful algal blooms page)
channels.note: NMED's bloom page (answered 200 on 2026-11-07) explains the WATCH, WARNING and DANGER advisories and links the advisory map; watched for a new map address, since the map's layer is named for its upload (Upload_Data_May2026). Blooms, not sewage. Voluntary.

channels.name: New Mexico Environment Department (news releases)
channels.note: NMED's news list (answered 200 on 2026-11-07): algal bloom advisories issued and lifted (a DANGER advisory at Charette Lake in 2026), boil water advisories and monthly enforcement summaries; no sewage overflow notice was seen.
